hints.title: Single Row In-Place Update Order
hints.text: Only a specific single row needs to be returned. How can updating elements in reverse order compute the next row in a single array?

hints.title: Reverse In-Place Overwrite Invariant
hints.text: Iterating right to left when updating row entries row[j] += row[j - 1] preserves the old row[j - 1] values without using extra arrays.

hints.title: Single Array Backward Accumulation Procedure
hints.text: Initialize a single array of size rowIndex + 1 with first element 1 and rest 0. For each step i from 1 to rowIndex, iterate backwards from i down to 1 setting row[j] = row[j] + row[j - 1]. Return the array.

hints.title: Complete Implementation

complexity.notes: Optimal solution achieving O(N^2) time and O(N) auxiliary space.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Maintaining the entire 2D triangle uses O(N^2) space when only O(N) space is required.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Updating a single 1D array backwards computes the rowIndex-th row in O(N^2) time using O(N) auxiliary space.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Candidate should demonstrate O(N) space optimization by updating elements from right to left.
